newsitem.title: USA: US safety board makes Embraer recommendations.
newsitem.headline: US safety board makes Embraer recommendations.

text.p: The National Transportation Safety Board on Wednesday made its own set of urgent recommendations to combat ice accumulation on Embraer EMB-120 aircraft.

Just over a week ago the Federal Aviation Administration proposed ordering the installation of ice detection systems on the Brazilian-made turbo-props and proposed changes to the flight manual on operating in icing conditions.

The NTSB said the FAA's proposal addressed many of the safety issues but the board's recommendations were, in some respects, more specific than the FAA's and would assist in obtaining industry acceptance.

In a letter to acting FAA Administrator Barry Valentine, NTSB Chairman James Hall said the board sought specific training in the plane's new de-icing procedures, because many flightcrews would need to "unlearn acquired practices."
The letter also said the board was evaluating whether the FAA's minimum speed recommendation for icing conditions was appropriate.
Icing is suspected in the crash of a Comair Embraer 120 on approach to Detroit Metropolitan Airport on January 9 of this year, killing all 29 people on board.
NTSB's letter described icing incidents going back to 1989 in support of its recommendations.
An FAA spokesman said the NTSB recommendations were being reviewed and noted that the FAA responded favorably to 90 percent of NTSB urgent recommendations.
The EMB-120 is manufactured by Empresa Brasileira de Aeronautica S.A.
